Literate programming, in the sense used here, means writing a scientific document in which narrative text, data, executable code and the code's output live in a single source file, so that the results reported are produced by the code shown. Tools for this include Emacs org-mode, MATLAB notebooks, and the IPython/Jupyter notebook. It supports [reproducibility](/papers/topics/reproducibility/) and [data sharing](/papers/topics/data-sharing/) because the published document carries its own data and analysis.

## An org-mode manuscript as supporting information (2014)

The paper on simulating oxygen TPD from Pt(111) was prepared as a single org-mode document holding the raw TPD data, the Python analysis that produced every figure, and the manuscript text; the LaTeX submission was exported from it, and the document itself was published as the supporting information ([Miller et al. 2013](/papers/miller2014/)). The authors present this as a way to make the full analysis transparent and reusable rather than treating supporting information as an afterthought. Summary: [miller2014](/papers/miller2014/).

## Org-mode for scientific manuscripts (2015)

Kitchin describes the group's practice of writing papers in org-mode, a near plain-text markup that distinguishes text, citations, equations, tables, images, code and data, and which Emacs can execute and export to PDF, LaTeX or HTML ([Kitchin 2015](/papers/kitchin2015/)). The Viewpoint was itself written this way, with its code listings run in the document and their output captured automatically. A key feature is that org tables are both rendered for human readers and addressable as data sources by code blocks, and because org is a parseable syntax, a short Python function can extract a named table without Emacs. The org source is attached to the Supporting Information PDF, so readers receive the data, code and narrative together. The author acknowledges a learning curve, compares it to learning LaTeX, and argues that copying code into LaTeX cannot guarantee it is the code that was run. Summary: [kitchin2015](/papers/kitchin2015/).

## Supporting Information as a data and code repository (2016)

This Prospective, itself written in org-mode and exported to LaTeX with executed code listings, shows an org table of experimental Cu core-level shifts that renders as an ordinary table yet can be read by a code block and replotted ([Kitchin 2016](/papers/kitchin2016a/)). It stresses that org code blocks remain executable, can be called from other org files, and can be tangled into standalone code, so a Supporting Information file can double as a code repository (a Python library is tangled from the Supporting Information of [boes2015a](/papers/boes2015a/)). The group reports nine publications prepared this way over two years. Summary: [kitchin2016a](/papers/kitchin2016a/).
